Method, so it can be repeated: copy test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs and json-schema-subset.mjs to a scratch directory, change COVERAGE_FLOOR to 1.01 so that every contract is reported rather than only the failing ones, and run `node --test --test-name-pattern="mutation-coverage floor" <copy>` from the repository root; the per-contract killed/total pairs are in the assertion message and the catalog figure is their sum. WHAT THE ENTRY WAS FOR STILL STANDS: a floor is not a target. 67 constraint sites across the catalog are killed by no fixture at all, and each one is a rule that nothing exercises. A 70% floor against a measured 90.7% leaves twenty points in which coverage can regress with nothing failing; what actually holds the line is the per-contract UNKILLED_CEILING and SITE_FLOOR tables, which are exact and must be edited deliberately. Raising the floor is still cheap and should still be done as coverage rises. One consequence for a reader of this list: the '82% coverage' figure quoted in the next-but-one entry predates this measurement and was left untouched because it was not re-measured.

Roughly 71% of the 441 generated counterexamples are MECHANICAL -- they violate a rule with a sentinel value (`zz not matching pattern`) rather than with a value a producer could plausibly emit. Independent testing measured it and the judgement is accepted: the 66 enum, pattern and format fixtures are the weakest, because those keywords are exactly where a contract encodes a specific hazard and a sentinel erases it. They are load-bearing -- each one is a real witness that kills exactly one site -- but they are not documentation, and 82% coverage should not be read as 82% of the catalog's hazards being illustrated.

RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD: catalog 654 of 721 constraint sites killed by a declared fixture = 90.7%; weakest contract ctr-ntf-001 at 30 of 39 = 76.9%. Method, so it can be repeated: copy test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs and json-schema-subset.mjs to a scratch directory, change COVERAGE_FLOOR to 1.01 so that every contract is reported rather than only the failing ones, and run `node --test --test-name-pattern="mutation-coverage floor" <copy>` from the repository root; the per-contract killed/total pairs are in the assertion message and the catalog figure is their sum. Nothing in the repository was edited to measure this. WHAT THE ENTRY WAS FOR STILL STANDS: a floor is not a target. 67 constraint sites across the catalog are killed by no fixture at all, and each one is a rule that nothing exercises. A 70% floor against a measured 90.7% leaves twenty points in which coverage can regress with nothing failing; what actually holds the line is the per-contract UNKILLED_CEILING and SITE_FLOOR tables, which are exact and must be edited deliberately. Raising the floor is still cheap and should still be done as coverage rises. One consequence for a reader of this list: the '82% coverage' figure quoted in the next-but-one entry predates this measurement and was left untouched because it was not re-measured.

Roughly 71% of the 441 generated counterexamples are MECHANICAL -- they violate a rule with a sentinel value (`zz not matching pattern`) rather than with a value a producer could plausibly emit. Independent testing measured it and the judgement is accepted: the 66 enum, pattern and format fixtures are the weakest, because those keywords are exactly where a contract encodes a specific hazard and a sentinel erases it. They are load-bearing -- each one is a real witness that kills exactly one site -- but they are not documentation, and 82% coverage should not be read as 82% of the catalog's hazards being illustrated.
